Predict with saved XGBoost fold models on Spark

Source: R/spark.R
predict_xgb_spark.Rd

Reads native .ubj booster files, predicts each fold on the supplied data, and averages folds within each resampling repeat. Predictors are assembled in the order retained during fitting. Results are written as one Parquet dataset with one prediction column per repeat, named from the model index.

Usage

predict_xgb_spark(
  master,
  home,
  workspace,
  database = "duckdb",
  input = NULL,
  models,
  pred = NULL
)

Arguments

master, home, workspace, database

Spark connection and configuration arguments passed as in fit_xgb_spark().

input

Character path or paths to prediction Parquet data. Data must contain site_id, time, lon, lat, and the saved predictor columns, with one row per site_id and time. No response column is required. Usable paths must be supplied despite the NULL default.

models

The complete model list returned by fit_xgb_spark(), supplied directly or read from a saved R object. Prediction uses index and the ordered xvar vector. The index must contain rset, fold, prediction, and path columns, with one native booster file per fold and one prediction-column name per repeat. Paths must be accessible to the Spark driver.

pred

character(1). Required output Parquet directory, written with overwrite mode. A usable path must be supplied despite the NULL default. The directory must be accessible to Spark and R and separate from input data and model files.

Value

A character vector of absolute .parquet part-file paths beneath pred, suitable for saving as a workflow input to a subsequent stage.

Details

Uses the same Spark and XGBoost JAR configuration as fit_xgb_spark(). Native boosters are wrapped as Spark regression models without reading Spark model metadata. Features are made dense to preserve zero values. Prediction covers all input rows, regardless of XGB_MAX_ROWS.

All indexed folds within each repeat contribute equally to its mean prediction. Repeat-specific tables are joined by site_id, time, lon, and lat. The saved dataset contains these identifiers and one prediction column per repeat, such as base_001 or meta_001. The Spark connection is disconnected on exit, including on error.

See also

fit_xgb_spark(), assemble_xgb_features()
